title: Beef, short loin, T‑bone steak, bone‑in, separable lean only, trimmed to 1/8" fat, choice, cooked, grilled

content.title: About
content.content: A T‑bone steak is a cut of beef that includes both the short loin (strip) and a portion of the tenderloin, separated by a T‑shaped bone. This version is trimmed to leave only a 1/8‑inch layer of fat, making it lean yet still flavorful. The “choice” grade indicates high quality, and grilling imparts a classic smoky char.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The T‑bone combines two of the most prized cuts—strip and tenderloin—in one steak.
The bone helps retain heat and juices during cooking, enhancing tenderness.
Historically, T‑bone steaks were cooked over open flames, linking them to early barbecue traditions.
In the United States, the T‑bone is often seen as an icon of American grilling culture.
Trimming to a 1/8‑inch fat cap provides a leaner product without sacrificing taste.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Provides about 25 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Rich source of iron
items.content: Contains heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Supplies B12, B6, and niacin, essential for nervous system function and energy metabolism.

items.title: Zinc and selenium
items.content: These trace minerals support immune health and antioxidant defenses.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Virtually carbohydrate‑free, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Even with a thin fat cap, the steak still contains saturated fats that should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Portion size
items.content: Large servings can add significant calories to the diet.

items.title: Potential pathogens
items.content: Insufficient grilling may leave harmful bacteria such as E. coli.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Rare, but some individuals may have an allergic reaction to beef.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Best served medium‑rare (55‑57 °C internal temperature) to retain juiciness. Slice across the grain, let rest 5‑10 minutes before serving. Pair with grilled vegetables, a red‑wine reduction, or a simple pat of butter.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the steak in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C for up to 3‑5 days. For longer storage, freeze at ‑18 °C, where it maintains quality for 6‑12 months. Thaw in the fridge, not at room temperature, before cooking.
